journal.canopy.heading: Field notes
journal.canopy.empty: The page is blank. A note appears when I see it myself.
journal.canopy.wet: The ink ran. I cannot read this until the book dries.
journal.canopy.now.venom: Bitter in the mouth. Milk does nothing. I wait it out.
journal.canopy.now.bleeding: The scratch still smells. The cats know it.
journal.canopy.now.thirst: No water. Two bamboo make a flask. The river is a poor drink raw.
journal.canopy.now.thirst_flask: The flask is here. Fill it from the river and boil it.
journal.canopy.now.food: Empty stomach. I will not eat the root raw. Fire first.
journal.canopy.now.food_fire: There is something to cook. Raw food goes on a lit fire.
journal.canopy.now.hot: The body cannot hold this heat. Shade, or take the hide off.
journal.canopy.now.cold: Wet and chilling. I need a fire.
journal.canopy.now.flood_warn: A rumble upstream. The water is not here yet. I need to climb. The bottom is no place to wait.
journal.canopy.now.flood_wave: The flow is on the bottom. My feet will not hold. Higher up is already dry.
journal.canopy.now.downpour: Downpour. Leaves are not a roof. Open fires die, and the ground sticks.
journal.canopy.now.downpour_roof: Downpour outside. This roof holds. Under the leaves I would be soaked.
journal.canopy.now.fever: Fever. The eyes blur, thirst goes faster, the body is weaker. Wash with clean water, then bind it.
journal.canopy.now.infected: The wound is hot around the edges. Clean water, then a bamboo strip. Food will not close it.
journal.canopy.now.wound_dirty: The wound is open and dirty. Crouch with a clean flask and wash it. Then the strip.
journal.canopy.now.wound: The wound is washed. A bamboo strip will close it. Food will not bring health all the way back.
journal.canopy.now.venom_brew: Bitter in the mouth. The brew of the bitter leaf, off the fire, takes it off.
journal.canopy.now.hand: The hand is raw. Three bamboo in a strip will bind it. Until then, leave the stone alone.
journal.canopy.now.wet_clothes: The clothes squelch. They dry by the fire.
journal.canopy.now.night: It is getting dark. Night is long without a fire.
journal.canopy.now.fire: By the fire I can eat and dry off.
journal.canopy.now.quiet: Quiet for now. Next is the thing I still cannot do.
journal.canopy.now.path_flask: First a flask. Bamboo grows in the thicket. Two stalks, one above the other. Fill from the river and boil it. Do not drink it raw.
journal.canopy.now.path_machete: Next the machete. Flint above bamboo. That is how I walk the thicket. It does not take stone.
journal.canopy.now.path_taro: I look for the broad leaf on the ground, in the lowland and by the water. I do not eat the root raw. It goes on a lit fire.
journal.canopy.now.path_fire: I need a campfire of logs and sticks. Water boils there, and food cooks. Night without it is cold.
journal.canopy.now.path_bandage: Three bamboo in a row make a strip. It binds the hand. A wound wants clean water first.
journal.canopy.now.path_tree: Silk hangs on a tree taller than the rest, in the lowland and up the slope. I climb the vine. There is none on the ground.
journal.canopy.now.path_canyon: Metal is in the open canyon wall, not underground. I do not dig: the air down there is heavy. The gouge is flint on a stick.
journal.canopy.now.path_river: The others went upriver. If I find their camp, the fire is cold. Until then I stay near water and a flame.
journal.canopy.plants.taro: A root with a broad leaf. I do not know its name. I have not eaten it.
journal.canopy.plants.taro_raw: Ate it raw. The stomach turned, and the hunger got worse. Not raw again.
journal.canopy.plants.taro_cooked: On the fire the root is food. Still not a full meal.
journal.canopy.plants.bitter: A bitter leaf. On the fire it becomes a brew. I will not mix it with food.
journal.canopy.plants.bad_brew: I mixed the leaf with taro. The stomach clenched. That is not medicine.
journal.canopy.plants.antidote: The brew off the fire takes off snake venom. It does not touch wound fever.
journal.canopy.beasts.jaguar: A big cat. It stayed still, then it jumped. It does not run straight.
journal.canopy.beasts.jaguar_bite: The claws went deep. I smell of blood for a long time after.
journal.canopy.beasts.agouti: Small and quick. The meat off it is raw and needs the fire.
journal.canopy.beasts.snake: A snake in the grass. It strikes if I stand close.
journal.canopy.beasts.snake_bite: The bite burns. Milk does not touch it. I wait until it lets go.
journal.canopy.beasts.monkey: Small ones, in the branches. They do not bite on their own.
journal.canopy.beasts.monkey_raid: They took one stack. The journal and what I am wearing stayed. Kill one and the stack can come back.
journal.canopy.places.bamboo_thicket: Bamboo like a wall. Flask and weave both come from it.
journal.canopy.places.canyon: Stone and a dry wash. A pickaxe does nothing useful here.
journal.canopy.places.flooded: Flooded ground. Water to the knee, the bottom is unsure.
journal.canopy.places.highland: Higher and a little cooler. The forest is thinner.
journal.canopy.places.downpour: The downpour caught me without a roof. Torches in the open drop. The ground sticks. The cats come closer.
journal.canopy.places.flood_wash: In the canyon the rumble comes first. Then water along the bottom. The wall stays dry.
journal.canopy.places.living_floor: The old deck creaked. I stepped off and it held. I stayed and it gave way. Below: muck, stakes, or a snake.
journal.canopy.places.bait: Someone else's pack, a strip of cloth on it. I took the hide. A branch cracked overhead and a cat dropped.
journal.canopy.places.canopy: A tree taller than the rest. Silk hangs at the top. There is none on the ground.
journal.canopy.places.vein: Metal glints in the open rock. A pick and bare hands only scratch it. It wants a narrow flint.
journal.canopy.places.camp: Someone else's camp. The fire is cold. In the bundle: a gouge, cloth, and a nugget. The note says they went upriver. The metal is in the canyon wall.
journal.canopy.places.gas: Underground, and by the dark mud, the air is heavy. Next to the pale shoot I can breathe. The filter buys a little over a minute, not a life down there.
journal.canopy.plants.air: A pale shoot. The air is lighter beside it. It does not make a cave safe by itself.
journal.canopy.now.gas: The air is heavy. I need to climb, or reach the shoot.
journal.canopy.now.gas_mask: The air is heavy. A filter of charcoal and bamboo.
journal.canopy.now.gas_filter: The filter holds. It will not hold long.
journal.canopy.craft.flask: Two bamboo, one above the other. A flask for the river. Boil it on the fire.
journal.canopy.craft.machete: Flint on bamboo. It takes the thicket, not the stone.
journal.canopy.craft.cooked: I put raw food on a lit fire. Then it can be eaten.
journal.canopy.craft.fiber: Bamboo on the skin. Cooler than going bare.
journal.canopy.craft.hide: Hide off the cat. Warm and thick. Stifling at noon.
journal.canopy.craft.bandage: Three bamboo in a strip. Clean water first, then the cloth. It will not lie on dirt. The hand it closes at once.
journal.canopy.craft.rope: Silk and bamboo. A rope for the trunk.
journal.canopy.craft.gouge: Flint on a stick. It takes the glint out of the rock. It will not cut a mountain.
journal.canopy.craft.metal: I set the nugget into the edge. The thicket goes easier. Stone still does not.
journal.canopy.craft.respirator: Charcoal from a log in a furnace, and bamboo on the face. It does not last.
advancement.canopy.field_notes.desc: The journal stays with me. Wet, it cannot be read.
item.canopy.bamboo_flask.hint.empty: Look at water and use the flask to fill it.
item.canopy.bamboo_flask.hint.murky: Barely helps, and it turns the stomach. Boil it on a lit campfire.
item.canopy.bamboo_flask.hint.clean: This water is safe to drink. Crouch and use it to wash a wound.
item.canopy.bamboo_flask.hint.fresh: From a bromeliad cup or a cut liana. Cleaner than the river, weaker than boiled.
item.canopy.log_fungus.hint: Grows on logs. Edible raw, barely.
message.canopy.liana_needs_machete: Lianas are cut with a machete: hold one in the other hand.
journal.canopy.plants.liana: Thick liana from the crown. Cut it with the machete and water pooled in the stem. It holds my weight too.
journal.canopy.plants.bromeliad: A rosette on a branch or log. After rain there is water inside, the flask takes it.
journal.canopy.plants.heliconia: Red crests on stalks. Birds visit them. Nothing to eat.
journal.canopy.plants.ginger: White flower where the mist and moss are. Sharp smell. Have not touched it yet.
journal.canopy.plants.fungus: Bracket fungus on a fallen trunk. Ate one, stomach held. Food for a bad day.
item.canopy.stone_machete.hint: Cuts thicket, bamboo, and vines. It does not bite stone.
message.canopy.hand_hurt: The hand is raw. A bamboo strip will bind it. Leave the stone alone until then.
advancement.canopy.cut_path.desc: The machete takes the thicket. Bare hands do not.
item.canopy.taro_root.hint: Raw, it turns the stomach. A lit campfire makes it food.
item.canopy.cooked_taro.hint: Edible. Still not a full meal.
item.canopy.raw_meat.hint: Spoils in a wet pack. It keeps beside a fire.
item.canopy.raw_meat.spoiling: The wet meat is starting to turn.
item.canopy.cooked_meat.hint: More filling than a root, and not for the whole day.
item.canopy.spoiled_meat.hint: Eating this is a bad idea.
advancement.canopy.cooked_meal.desc: Raw food from the fire can be eaten. A full stomach is still far off.
journal.canopy.beasts.capybara: Big rodent by the water. Not afraid until you get close. Plenty of meat, slips into the river.
journal.canopy.beasts.tapir: Dark, with a short trunk. Went through the thicket like it was grass. Saw me and left. A week of food, if I could catch it.
journal.canopy.beasts.caiman: Lies in the water like a log. The log opened its eyes. No more wading in to the waist.
journal.canopy.beasts.caiman_bite: Took my leg at the bank. The wound is torn and dirty. Wash it now.
journal.canopy.beasts.gorilla: Big, black, on the slope in the mist. They watch. As long as I kept my distance they left me alone.
journal.canopy.beasts.gorilla_hit: Got too close. One blow knocked me off my feet. Their ground, not mine.
journal.canopy.beasts.toucan: Black bird with a huge bill. Calls from the canopy in the morning. It tells me where the fruit is.
item.canopy.fiber.hint: Quiet and cool. It barely turns a claw.
item.canopy.hide.hint: It holds a bite. It is hot, wet, and loud.
message.canopy.bleeding: The blood has a smell. The cats know it.
message.canopy.wound_open: The wound is open and dirty. The cats smell it until I close it.
message.canopy.washed: Washed with clean water. Now it can be bound.
message.canopy.wash_late: Washed, but the wound is already hot. The strip is still needed.
message.canopy.murky_wound: Raw water in the wound. That only makes it dirtier.
message.canopy.bandage_close: The strip is on. The wound is closed.
message.canopy.bandage_dirty: Cloth will not lie on dirt. Clean water first.
message.canopy.infected: The wound is hot. A little longer and the fever starts.
message.canopy.brewed: The leaf boiled down. A bitter brew, not food.
message.canopy.antidote: The bitterness took the venom off.
message.canopy.antidote_spare: Drank it for nothing. There was no venom.
message.canopy.bad_brew: The stomach clenched. That is not medicine.
message.canopy.downpour: Downpour. Open fires die, and the ground sticks.
message.canopy.raid_empty: They lingered and left. There was nothing to carry.
message.canopy.flood_warn: A rumble upstream. There is time to climb.
message.canopy.flood_wave: Water on the bottom. It takes the feet out.
message.canopy.flood_high: The flow passed below. It is dry here.
message.canopy.deck_creak: The deck creaked. I need to step off.
message.canopy.deck_bog: The deck gave way. Muck below.
message.canopy.deck_stakes: The deck gave way. Stakes below.
message.canopy.deck_snake: The deck gave way. A snake below.
item.canopy.stone_gouge.hint: A narrow flake. It takes metal from a vein. It will not cut a mountain.
item.canopy.metal_machete.hint: An edge from a nugget. The thicket is easier. Stone still is not.
item.canopy.respirator.hint: Charcoal and bamboo. It wears away in bad air. Clean air does not spend it.
message.canopy.gas_filter: The filter holds. Not for long.
command.canopy.gas_blocked: No ground here for the seep.
message.canopy.camp_open: The fire is cold. The bundle holds someone else's things.
command.canopy.vein_blocked: No rock here to cut a vein into.
command.canopy.bait_blocked: No room to set the pack down.
advancement.canopy.gave_way.desc: The old deck did not hold. There was a pit under it.
advancement.canopy.from_above.desc: The marked pack was someone else's. A cat dropped from above.
advancement.canopy.high_silk.desc: The silk only hangs in the crown. I had to climb.
advancement.canopy.pried.desc: A nugget came out of the exposed vein. A pick had nothing to do with it.
advancement.canopy.left_behind.desc: The fire was already cold. They went upriver and left the bundle.
advancement.canopy.filtered.desc: The charcoal filter held in the heavy air. Not for long.
death.attack.canopy.flood: %1$s was swept away by the flood
advancement.canopy.downpour.desc: A downpour in the open. Fires die, and the ground sticks.
advancement.canopy.light_fingers.desc: The monkeys took a stack. The journal and what I wear stayed.
advancement.canopy.high_ground.desc: The rumble warned me. The flow stayed on the bottom.
item.canopy.bandage.hint: Three bamboo. Closes a washed wound and a raw hand.
item.canopy.bitter_herb.hint: On a lit fire it becomes a brew. With taro it becomes junk.
item.canopy.bad_brew.hint: A leaf mixed with food. It poisons and cures nothing.
item.canopy.antidote.hint: Takes off snake venom. It does not touch wound fever.
advancement.canopy.bound.desc: Clean water, then the strip. The wound is closed.
advancement.canopy.antidote.desc: The brew off the fire took off snake venom.
message.canopy.milk: Milk does not touch this venom.
advancement.canopy.small_game.desc: An agouti feeds you better than bare hands on stone.
advancement.canopy.woven.desc: Bamboo on the skin beats bare skin in the sun.
message.canopy.blackout.carried: You come to. Something small dragged you: the tracks on your sleeve are not yours.
message.canopy.blackout.left: You woke where you fell. This time, nobody came.
advancement.canopy.clean_water.desc: The river barely helps. Fire does.
item.canopy.bone_shard.hint: A sharp splinter of bone. Two in a column over bamboo make a bone machete.
item.canopy.bone_machete.hint: Longer than the stone one and holds an edge better. It clears the thicket.
item.canopy.rubber_sap.hint: Milky sap of the rubber tree. In the grid with a garment it waxes it — the cloth barely gets wet.
item.canopy.stilt_platform.hint: Stilts reach the bottom through four blocks. A camp over water and mire.
item.canopy.hammock.hint: Hangs between two anchors: trunks, a wall or platform posts. Sleeping in it sets your camp.
item.canopy.stew.hint: Thick and hot. Feeds you a day ahead.
message.canopy.wet_season: The sky grows heavy. The wet season begins: rain for days, water rising twice as often.
message.canopy.dry_season: The clouds part. The wet season is over.
message.canopy.hammock_loose: Nothing to hang the hammock on: the ends must reach trunks or platform posts.
message.canopy.rubber_dry: The cut is fresh, the sap has not welled up. Come back later.
message.canopy.oven_need_fire: There is food in the oven, but no fire beneath.
message.canopy.oven_empty: One portion in the oven. It needs at least one more.
message.canopy.oven_cooking: The stew is on the fire. Almost ready.
journal.canopy.craft.bone: A big beast's bone cuts the thicket longer than flint. Two shards in a column over bamboo — a machete above the stone one.
journal.canopy.craft.rubber: A knot sits low on the smooth trunks. The gouge draws milky sap from it. It keeps the cloth from soaking.
journal.canopy.craft.stew: Over the fire, roots and meat in the clay pot turn into thick stew. One bowl — and the day is fed.
journal.canopy.places.wet_season: The season of wet days: downpours come twice as often and the canyon water warns twice as much.
journal.canopy.places.camp_built: A platform on stilts and a hammock — a camp. Sleep, and you come back here. Rivers and mires stop being walls.
journal.canopy.hover_tip: Hover a mark — the journal will tell.
journal.canopy.node.craft_flask.desc: A bamboo stalk holds water. Drink from rivers, rain, bromeliads.
journal.canopy.node.craft_flask.hint: You need something to carry water in.
journal.canopy.node.craft_machete.desc: Flint bound to bamboo. Cuts branches, lianas and leaf litter.
journal.canopy.node.craft_machete.hint: Bare hands won't clear this brush.
journal.canopy.node.craft_gouge.desc: A flint chisel. Opens ore veins in rock and taps rubber trees.
journal.canopy.node.craft_rope.desc: Bamboo and silk from canopy pods. Holds decking and the hammock.
journal.canopy.node.craft_rope.hint: Silk hangs somewhere in the crowns.
journal.canopy.node.craft_bone.desc: Shards from large beasts cut straighter and longer than flint.
journal.canopy.node.craft_metal.desc: Veins in exposed canyon rock — metal without a mine.
journal.canopy.node.place_camp_built.des: Stilt decking and a hammock between anchors. Sleep sets your return point.
journal.canopy.node.place_camp_built.hin: You can build a home over water.
journal.canopy.node.craft_fiber.desc: Light, breathes in the heat. Weak armor, but better than bare skin.
journal.canopy.node.craft_hide.desc: Jaguar and gorilla hides — protection on par with iron armor.
journal.canopy.node.craft_rubber.desc: Rubber-tree sap on clothing — rain just beads off.
journal.canopy.node.craft_bandage.desc: Bamboo cloth with bitter leaf. Stops bleeding; dirty wounds take longer.
journal.canopy.node.craft_cooked.desc: Raw roots burn the mouth. Over fire they become food.
journal.canopy.node.craft_stew.desc: A clay pot over fire cooks several servings at once. Filling for a long time.
journal.canopy.node.craft_stew.hint: Roots and meat go better together.
journal.canopy.node.antidote.desc: Bitter leaf in a flask of clean water. Clears venom and fever heat.
journal.canopy.node.antidote.hint: There's a herb for snake venom.
journal.canopy.node.craft_respirator.des: An air plant inside a bandage filters gas-pocket spores.
journal.canopy.node.taro_seen.desc: Heart-shaped leaves hide a root. Raw it burns, cooked it feeds.
journal.canopy.node.taro_cooked.desc: Fire takes the bite out. Plain jungle food.
journal.canopy.node.bitter_seen.desc: Sharp toothed leaves. In bandages and brews — against venom and infection.
journal.canopy.node.air_plant.desc: A pale rosette near gas pockets. A filter for your lungs.
journal.canopy.node.air_plant.hint: Where air is bad, the filter grows.
journal.canopy.node.plant_liana.desc: Climbable. Cut with a machete and the stem runs with water.
journal.canopy.node.plant_bromeliad.desc: A trunk-side rosette collecting rainwater. Your flask drinks straight from the leaves.
journal.canopy.node.plant_bromeliad.hint: Cups of water grow on trees.
journal.canopy.node.plant_heliconia.desc: Bright crests. Yields red dye and livens a camp.
journal.canopy.node.plant_ginger.desc: White blooms, a spicy root — seasoning and mild medicine.
journal.canopy.node.plant_fungus.desc: Orange shelves on trunks. Food off the tree, if you find it.
journal.canopy.node.beast_agouti.desc: A quick rodent of the understory. Small game — meat for supper.
journal.canopy.node.beast_monkey.desc: Steals shiny things and hauls them to the crowns. Follow for its stash.
journal.canopy.node.beast_toucan.desc: Noisy crown bird. Bright feathers for show and bait.
journal.canopy.node.beast_capybara.desc: A calm giant by the water. Plenty of meat and bones, fears almost nothing.
journal.canopy.node.beast_capybara.hint: Something big grazes by the water.
journal.canopy.node.beast_tapir.desc: Spotted as a calf, dark as an adult. Meat, bones, thick hide.
journal.canopy.node.beast_tapir.hint: Strange tracks lead to the stream.
journal.canopy.node.beast_snake.desc: Hides in grass and strikes at ankles. Venom burns — bitter leaf saves.
journal.canopy.node.beast_caiman.desc: A waterside ambush. Grabs and tears — wounds run deep. Tough hide.
journal.canopy.node.beast_caiman.hint: Not every log in the water is a log.
journal.canopy.node.beast_jaguar.desc: Hunter of the thickets. Hits hard, leaves bleeding wounds. The hide is the best armor.
journal.canopy.node.beast_jaguar.hint: A shadow breathes in the bushes.
journal.canopy.node.beast_gorilla.desc: Families deep in the forest. Leave them be; anger them and they hit like hammers.
journal.canopy.node.beast_gorilla.hint: Something beats its chest deep inside.
journal.canopy.node.place_lowland.desc: Tall trees, dense underbrush. The jungle's main home.
journal.canopy.node.place_lowland.hint: The jungle around is not all the same.
journal.canopy.node.place_bamboo_thicket: Walls of bamboo, dry litter. Fast materials — and tight quarters.
journal.canopy.node.place_flooded.desc: Knee-deep water, mangrove roots, caimans. Build on stilts only.
journal.canopy.node.place_highland.desc: Moss and lichen on trunks, spore blooms, cooler air.
journal.canopy.node.place_highland.hint: Higher up the forest breathes differently.
journal.canopy.node.place_canyon.desc: Walls of terracotta and silt strata, open rock, metal veins.
journal.canopy.node.place_canopy.desc: In giant crowns — silk pods. Ropes, clothing, the hammock.
journal.canopy.node.place_canopy.hint: Some trees stand taller than the rest.
journal.canopy.node.place_vein.desc: Canyon rock shows metal. Chisel out ingots without a mine.
journal.canopy.node.place_gas.desc: Cracks seep spores. Without a respirator — coughing and rotten lungs.
journal.canopy.node.place_downpour.desc: The sky opens at once. Dry under the crowns, soaked to the bone in the open.
journal.canopy.node.place_downpour.hint: Rain here has its own temper.
journal.canopy.node.place_flood.desc: After downpours water comes in waves. The canyon and swamp flood first.
journal.canopy.node.place_flood.hint: The river knows how to rise.
journal.canopy.node.place_wet_season.des: Weeks of rain. Floods come often, fires die out; stew and decking save you.
journal.canopy.node.place_wet_season.hin: The sky can change its mood.
journal.canopy.node.place_camp.desc: Someone else's traces: cargo in cane, rotten decking. Strip it — it's useful.
journal.canopy.node.plant_banana.desc: Bunches ripen under the canopy. A ripe one comes off by hand — quick sweet food.
journal.canopy.node.plant_banana.hint: Something yellow hangs under the leaves.
journal.canopy.node.plant_orchid.desc: Magenta on trunks and moss. Its flowers make purple dye.
item.canopy.banana.hint: Ripe and sweet. Picked in bunches under the canopy.
